page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-96-lssd is an x86_64 instance type from the Network Optimized family, engineered for demanding enterprise deployments that require significant memory density and high-throughput local storage. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 744 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of memory per core. Compute operations are handled exclusively by dedicated x86_64 processing threads, with no attached GPU acceleration.

A central component of this configuration is its integrated direct-attached storage tier, consisting of 16 local NVMe SSD drives that together supply 6,442 GB of disk capacity. This colocation of substantial memory capacity and high-capacity low-latency NVMe media eliminates common external storage bottlenecks, facilitating intensive input and output patterns directly on the host.

From a resource and cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets scale-up designs where consolidating multi-core CPU capacity, high memory allocation, and large NVMe disk volumes onto a single instance simplifies architecture. The absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses requires integration with internal virtual networks, private NAT gateways, or dedicated IP management.

This server type is suitable for large in-memory databases, high-performance transactional data stores, massive analytics caching layers, distributed ETL engines, and latency-sensitive data science processing pipelines requiring rapid scratch space.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-96-lssd is a network-optimized server powered by an x86_64 architecture featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 744 GB of system memory, delivering roughly 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built without GPU acceleration, the platform addresses intense data processing and storage demands by bundling 16 local NVMe solid-state drives totaling 6,442 GB of high-speed local disk capacity. The dense resource ratio pairs massive working memory directly with fast local block storage, eliminating network storage transfer delays for large-scale host-centric operations. It includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, favoring private cloud VPC network designs. This profile is engineered to handle large transactional database systems, massive in-memory analytics platforms, high-throughput caching engines, and demanding data science workflows requiring substantial local scratch performance.
